seo.title: Portfolio Intelligence | Portfolio Structure Review | DNH
seo.description: Assess portfolio composition, asset roles, concentration, liquidity and data quality to identify areas requiring review.

sections.heading: Portfolio Intelligence: understand your capital structure more clearly
paragraphs: Holding a variety of assets does not necessarily create a balanced portfolio. Capital allocation, concentration, liquidity and the role of each asset need to be considered together.
Drawing on Dr Nasim Mohammadhassani’s specialist approach, DNH reviews the existing portfolio structure to clarify concentrations and areas that may require attention.

sections.heading: Does your portfolio genuinely have an appropriate structure?
paragraphs: You may have invested across several markets over time, yet separate decisions do not always produce a coherent whole.
Before adding another asset, it may be more useful to review the structure already in place.

items.title: Excessive concentration
items.description: A large share of capital sits in one asset, market or industry.

items.title: Unclear asset roles
items.description: It is unclear whether each asset is held for growth, income, preservation or liquidity.

items.title: Shared risk drivers
items.description: Different assets may still depend on the same economic factor.

items.title: Mismatch with financial needs
items.description: The asset mix may not align with your objectives or the timing of future capital needs.

sections.heading: What can a portfolio-structure assessment reveal?
paragraphs: The review clarifies relationships between assets, concentrations and liquidity constraints.
The following conceptual example shows how that review may be framed.
sections.badge: DEMO | HYPOTHETICAL EXAMPLE, NOT A DNH CLIENT REPORT

items.title: Asset composition
items.description: How much capital is allocated to each asset class?

items.title: Concentration and common risk
items.description: Do several assets depend on similar economic factors?

items.title: Liquidity
items.description: Which parts of the portfolio are easier to access when needed?

items.title: Valuation quality
items.description: How current, reliable and realisable are the stated asset values?

sections.closing: Strategic question: is the current capital mix aligned with the owner’s needs and time horizon?
sections.note: Illustrative position: an individual holds property, equities, gold and cash. This example explains the review logic only and uses no real client data or findings.

sections.heading: What does a portfolio assessment examine?
paragraphs: Portfolio Intelligence examines assets as parts of one structure rather than isolated investments.
The scope is defined by the assets involved, available information and financial objectives.

items.title: Capital structure and composition
items.description: How capital is distributed across asset classes.

items.title: Asset roles
items.description: The role of each asset in growth, income, preservation or liquidity.

items.title: Concentration and common risk
items.description: Dependencies on similar markets or economic factors.

items.title: Liquidity
items.description: Access to capital when it is required.

items.title: Objectives and time horizon
items.description: The fit between the capital mix and short- or long-term needs.

items.title: Sufficiency of information
items.description: Data quality, valuation dates and assessment limitations.

sections.closing: The purpose is to clarify the existing portfolio and identify matters that may warrant review.

sections.heading: Who can benefit from a portfolio-structure assessment?
sections.intro: As assets and investment decisions become more varied, understanding the mix and shared risk drivers becomes increasingly important.

items.title: Individuals and investors
items.description: You invest across several markets and want a clearer view of composition, concentration and liquidity.

items.title: Families and wealth owners
items.description: You hold diverse assets and want to assess their fit with financial needs and future plans.

items.title: Business owners
items.description: Part of your capital is tied to a business and you want to understand its relationship with personal assets.

sections.heading: What role does each asset play in the portfolio?
sections.intro: Value and return alone are not enough. Each allocation should be considered in relation to portfolio risk, liquidity and objectives.

items.title: Gold
items.description: Its potential preservation role and sensitivity to economic conditions.

items.title: Currencies
items.description: Currency risk and the impact of exchange-rate movements.

items.title: Equities
items.description: Growth potential alongside volatility and market risk.

items.title: Property
items.description: Capital concentration and liquidity constraints.

items.title: Fixed income
items.description: Periodic income alongside credit, inflation and liquidity risks.

items.title: Cash and liquid resources
items.description: Access to funds and financial flexibility.

items.title: Commodities
items.description: Exposure to economic cycles and global markets.

items.title: Alternative assets
items.description: Asset-specific risk, liquidity and constraints.

sections.closing: This is not a ranking of assets to buy; it is a review of the roles played by assets already held.

sections.heading: Asset variety does not always create genuine risk diversification
paragraphs: Capital may be spread across several assets while all remain exposed to one economic change.
A high-value portfolio may also offer insufficient liquidity when funds are needed.

items.title: Single-asset concentration
items.description: A material share of capital depends on the value of one asset.

items.title: Common market risk
items.description: Several assets may respond to the same economic factor.

items.title: Liquidity constraints
items.description: Converting certain assets into cash may take time.

items.title: Timing mismatch
items.description: Access to capital does not align with obligations and financial goals.

sections.closing: The review distinguishes visible asset variety from genuine diversification of risk.

sections.heading: A recorded asset value is not always a realisable value
sections.intro: Approximate values are not enough. Valuation dates, saleability, transfer restrictions and information quality all affect the reliability of an assessment.

items.title: Valuation date
items.description: When was each asset last valued?

items.title: Realisable value
items.description: Could the asset be sold at the estimated value under real market conditions?

items.title: Transfer and sale constraints
items.description: What costs or restrictions may affect access to the asset’s value?

items.title: Information sufficiency and reliability
items.description: Is the available data usable, or does it require further work?

sections.closing: Where data or valuation is insufficient, the resulting limitations and uncertainty must be stated clearly.

sections.heading: How sensitive is the portfolio if economic conditions change?
sections.intro: Portfolio quality is not revealed only in normal conditions. Scenario review can expose sensitivities and structural constraints.

items.title: Higher inflation
items.description: Which allocations may be more exposed to declining purchasing power?

items.title: Currency volatility
items.description: How could exchange-rate changes affect asset values and relationships?

items.title: Lower market liquidity
items.description: How much flexibility remains if asset sales become difficult?

items.title: Changing market conditions
items.description: Which allocations are more sensitive if several markets move at once?

sections.closing: The aim is not to predict prices, but to identify conditions that could place the existing structure under pressure.

sections.heading: Portfolio assessment begins with the structure already in place
paragraphs: The specialist review is based on available information and individual circumstances.
Before work begins, the scope, required information and intended outputs are agreed.

items.title: Initial assessment
items.description: Clarify the issue, financial objectives and fit with Portfolio Intelligence.

items.title: Review available information
items.description: Identify asset classes and assess information sufficiency and valuation limitations.

items.title: Assess portfolio structure
items.description: Review composition, asset roles and concentrations.

items.title: Review risk and liquidity
items.description: Identify dependencies, timing constraints and economic sensitivity.

items.title: Conclude and prioritise
items.description: Clarify matters requiring review and the possible next stage of specialist work.

sections.note: This service is not automated account aggregation, real-time monitoring or algorithmic portfolio management.

sections.heading: What becomes clearer after the portfolio assessment?
sections.intro: The purpose is not to generate more information, but to produce a clearer view of the portfolio and the matters that affect the next decision.

groups.label: SERVICE POSITION
groups.title: How it differs from other DNH services
bullets: Wealth Architecture: assets, ownership, obligations and goals
Risk Management: vulnerabilities affecting the wider wealth structure
Portfolio Intelligence: existing asset mix, roles, concentration and liquidity

sections.note: This service does not provide trading signals, execute trades, manage a portfolio or guarantee performance. Output format and detail are agreed before specialist work begins.

sections.heading: Understand the current portfolio before making the next investment
paragraphs: If you hold diverse assets but remain uncertain about composition, concentration or liquidity, an initial assessment can be a useful starting point.
If the request is suitable and both parties agree, the specialist scope and next step will be defined.
sections.closing: You do not need to provide account credentials or confidential asset details at the initial stage.
